t: LeetCode 2124 - Check if All A's Appears Before All B's: The Forbidden "ba"
o: **Understanding the problem.** The string uses only 'a' and 'b', and it is valid precisely when all 'a's occupy a prefix and all 'b's fill the remaining suffix - solid blocks, never interleaved. "aaabbb" splits cleanly at index 3, so every 'a' precedes every 'b' and the answer is true. "abab" alternates: the 'b' at index 1 sits before the 'a' at index 2, so we return false. "bbb" contains no 'a' at all; the condition is vacuously satisfied, so it is true. With at most 100 characters, a single linear scan is all the constraints demand.
k: Validity fails exactly when a 'b' occurs somewhere before an 'a' - i.e. the substring "ba" exists.
Equivalently: after the first 'b' is seen, every later character must also be 'b'.
Strings made of a single letter (including "bbb") are vacuously valid.

a.i: Walk left to right remembering whether a 'b' has already appeared. The moment an 'a' shows up after that, the ordering is broken. Otherwise the whole string is one block of 'a's followed by one block of 'b's.
s: Iterate over s: if the current character is 'b', set seenB = true.
If the current character is 'a' and seenB is true, return false.
Return true after the loop completes.
a.t: O(n) - one pass over the string

a.i: The violation pattern is exactly the two-character substring "ba": a 'b' immediately followed by an 'a'. Every invalid string contains it and every valid string avoids it, so the whole scan can be delegated to the language's built-in substring search.
s: Return true if it is absent, false otherwise.
a.t: O(n) - the substring search inspects at most n starting positions

w: Present the flag scan first - it demonstrates you understand the structure - then close with the one-liner "no occurrence of ba" as a bonus remark. Vacuous cases (no 'a', no 'b', a single character) are all true; do not accidentally reject them. Likely follow-ups: generalize to a larger ordered alphabet by tracking the largest symbol seen so far, or compute the minimum number of edits to fix an invalid string (related to counting "ba" inversions).
